items.answer: Middleware is software that sits between hardware and higher-level application software, abstracts hardware functionalities for developers, and supports the development and rendering of extended reality (XR) experiences.
Human factors is the system-design consideration that requires knowing users’ differing expectations, needs, skills, and how they perceive stimuli, so that suitable input and output can be designed.

Interactive system is a system in which interaction takes place between the computer or system and the user, a lay person who is not necessarily a technology expert and who wants to use the system rather than understand how it works.

A user-centric approach is the process of designing computer systems in which users' needs and expectations are taken care of by considering user characteristics, starting with understanding those characteristics, needs, and expectations, then designing the system on that basis.

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

questions.question: In what way does the novice, intermittent, and expert categorization reduce reliance on initial field studies?
options: It gives designers a broad starting point for design decisions
It gives designers an exact, fine-grained user profile for design decisions
It gives designers a final, permanent user specification for design decisions
It gives designers a complete set of empirical findings for design decisions
questions.explanation: The three user classes are a broad early basis for design decisions. They are useful when design starts, but they are not an exact or final replacement for empirical user studies.

questions.question: What does the expert user class refer to in the novice, intermittent, and expert classification?
options: A person who is expert in testing that system
A person who is expert in using that system
A person who is expert in building that system
A person who is expert in the technology behind that system
questions.explanation: An expert user is expert in using the system efficiently. The term does not mean that the person is a technology expert or that they build or test the system.

questions.question: In the three-class user model, what distinguishes an intermittent user from an expert user?
options: First-time use versus occasional use
Occasional use versus regular long-term use
Occasional use versus regular short-term use
First-time use versus regular long-term use
questions.explanation: An intermittent user uses the system occasionally, while an expert user uses it regularly over a long period. First-time use describes a novice user.

questions.question: For a novice user saving a file, what makes a menu option more suitable than a hotkey option?
options: Difficulty remembering the hotkey option
Easier recall of the hotkey option
Faster execution of the menu option
Greater familiarity with the hotkey option
questions.explanation: A menu option can be more suitable for first-time users because remembering hotkey combinations is generally difficult for them. The menu option is not faster than the hotkey option.

data.text: Interactive-system design can use a practical shortcut for understanding users: a broad novice, intermittent, and expert classification. Because field studies are costly, designers can begin from that classification. It helps make early design decisions by recognizing likely differences in user behavior, for example in choosing menu or hotkey support. It remains a starting point, not a replacement for more detailed empirical studies.
points: Field studies are time-consuming and laborious, so designers can use the novice, intermittent, and expert categorization.
The classes are novice first-time users, intermittent occasional users, and expert long-term, efficient system users, not technology experts.
Because user classes behave differently, these classes give designers a starting point for broad interactive-system design decisions.
Applications can offer slower menu and faster hotkey options, matching menu to novices and hotkeys to intermittent and expert users.
This categorization is broad and useful at design start, though finer empirical studies can produce better user categorizations.

questions.question: Which stakeholder is mainly concerned with the product's shape, size, and look?
options: The electronic engineer
The user interface or user experience designer
The application software developer
The industrial product designer
questions.explanation: User-centric design means different things to different stakeholders; for an industrial product designer it concerns the product's form, such as its shape, size, and look. The other roles focus on interface design, hardware features, or a user-aware software lifecycle.

questions.question: How does an application software developer incorporate user characteristics into a VR or AR system?
options: By designing the product's shape, size, and external appearance
By choosing hardware-level features such as sensors and efficient batteries
By following a lifecycle that accounts for users' characteristics, needs, and expectations
By making creative choices about interface elements and layouts
questions.explanation: An application software developer builds user awareness into the system through a development or design lifecycle that takes user characteristics, needs, and expectations into account. The other options describe concerns of other stakeholder roles rather than the software developer's method.

data.text: User-centric design changes with the designer role, from interface elements to product form to hardware features. For an application software developer building a VR or AR system, this means following a lifecycle that keeps user characteristics, needs, and expectations in view. That user-aware development makes the system easier to use and better matched to those users.
points: User-centric design varies by role: interface elements for UI/UX designers, product form for product designers, hardware features for electronic engineers.
Application software developers follow a user-aware lifecycle so VR or AR systems better match user characteristics, needs, and expectations.

questions.question: What does usability explicitly measure?
options: how good a system is from the user's point of view
how fast a system can render an environment from the developer's point of view
how immersive a virtual experience is from the observer's point of view
how complete a product's feature set is from the designer's point of view
questions.explanation: Usability is an explicit user-point-of-view measure of how good a system is. It is not primarily a measure of features, rendering speed, or immersion.

questions.question: For a product to have usability under the formal definition, which three elements are specified?
options: the speed, the satisfaction, and the context of use
the novices, the intermittent users, and the expert users
the users, the goals, and the context of use
the users, the features, and the hardware
questions.explanation: The formal usability definition ties a product to particular users, particular goals, and a particular context of use. User classes, features, hardware, speed, and satisfaction are not the three specified elements.

questions.question: If a user can reach a goal and can reach it quickly, which usability measure has not yet been established?
options: Efficiency
Usability
Satisfaction
Effectiveness
questions.explanation: Reaching the goal addresses effectiveness, and reaching it quickly addresses efficiency. Satisfaction concerns how satisfied the user is while using the system, which is still a separate usability measure.

data.text: Usability gives an explicit user-based way to judge how good a system is. The ISO definition bounds that judgment by specifying the users, the goals, and the context of use. Within those bounds, effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction measure whether users can achieve what they want, how fast they can do it, and how satisfied they are.
points: Usability is an explicit measure of how good a system is from the user's point of view.
ISO usability is the extent specified users can use a product to achieve specified goals in a specified context.
Usability is measured by effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction: whether users succeed, how fast, and how satisfied.

questions.question: In the design approach that centers the person who will use the software, what kind of lifecycle involvement does it specify?
options: Direct operation of hardware in the lifecycle
Rendering of output data in the lifecycle
Active or passive participation in the lifecycle
Final approval of requirements in the lifecycle
questions.explanation: User-centered design involves users actively or passively in the design or development lifecycle. Final approval, hardware operation, and rendering are not the specified involvement.

questions.question: What outcome is the objective of user-centered design?
options: Products that increase immersion
Products that increase hardware efficiency
Products that increase feature count
Products that increase usability
questions.explanation: The objective of user-centered design is to design products that increase usability.

questions.question: What do cooperative design, participatory design, contextual design, and human-centered design have in common?
options: They involve interactive systems in the design process
They involve context of use in the design process
They involve users in the design process
They involve requirements in the design process
questions.explanation: These related terms refer to taking users into the design process, not requirements, systems, or the context of use as the central participant.

questions.question: What is the core design concern of user-centric software design?
options: Usable systems for lay users
Usable systems for pilgrim users
Usable systems for tourist users
Usable systems for student users
questions.explanation: The core concern is usable systems for lay persons or layman users in general, not a particular user group.

data.text: User-centered design is a user-centric approach that involves users in a design or development lifecycle used to build usable software. Ben Shneiderman coined the term in 1986 for graphical user interfaces, and its objective is to create usable systems that meet lay users’ needs and expectations. Cooperative, participatory, contextual, and human-centered design are related terms for taking users into design, with ISO preferring human-centered design.
points: User-centered design applies a user-centric approach and involves users in a design or development lifecycle to build usable software.
Ben Shneiderman coined user-centered design in 1986 for graphical user interfaces.
User-centered design aims to design usable systems that meet lay users’ needs and expectations.
Cooperative, participatory, contextual, and human-centered design are related terms for taking users into design; ISO prefers human-centered over user-centered design.

items.title: Order the related design terms in the order they were introduced
steps: User-centered design is introduced by Ben Shneiderman
Cooperative design is introduced by Greenbaum and Kyng

questions.question: What is the core concern of XR software?
options: track the user's actions and positions in the virtual environment
render the user's actions and positions in the virtual environment
create a relationship between the user and the virtual environment
swap out the user's real-world surroundings with the virtual environment
questions.explanation: The core concern of XR software is to build the relationship between the user and the virtual environment. Rendering or tracking user actions are parts of an XR pipeline, and replacing the real world describes a VR experience rather than the software's core concern.

questions.question: In an XR system, which component uses hardware resources to generate output data?
options: The application layer generates the output data
The output device generates the output data
The XR engine generates the output data
The input device generates the output data
questions.explanation: The XR engine, as middleware, uses hardware resources to generate output data. Input devices provide input data and output devices stimulate the senses, while the application layer does not fill that generation role.

questions.question: Why should user input modeling in an XR system follow a user-centered design approach?
options: so the user can provide the input seamlessly, effectively, and easily
so the hardware can capture the input seamlessly, effectively, and easily
so the engine can process the input seamlessly, effectively, and easily
so the user can perceive the output seamlessly, effectively, and easily
questions.explanation: User-centered design for interaction and input modeling exists so that the user can provide input data seamlessly, effectively, and easily. Perceiving output is the concern of perceptual design, while engine processing and hardware capture are separate roles from making user input easy.

questions.question: Why does perceptual design in an XR system require a user-centered approach?
options: so the generated output stimuli match the user's perception
so the used hardware resources match the user's perception
so the tracked user actions match the user's perception
so the processed input data match the user's perception
questions.explanation: Perceptual design must align the generated output stimuli with how the user perceives them, so the user can perceive and understand the output. Tracked actions, processed input data, and hardware resources are not the stimuli that perceptual design aligns with user perception.

data.text: XR is treated as an interactive system because users act on and receive feedback from a virtual environment. Hardware, the XR engine, and the application layer track user actions, render the environment, and stimulate the senses, so software and hardware together shape the user–environment relationship. Because this relationship depends on how users give input and perceive output, user-centered design is needed for both interaction and perception.
points: User-centered software development involves users actively or passively in the chosen software development lifecycle.
XR systems are highly interactive, making human factors important for how easily users provide input and perceive output.
XR software’s core concern is creating a relationship between the user and virtual environment, with software and hardware both important.
XR system components (hardware, XR engine, application) track user input, render the environment, and stimulate the senses through output devices.
User-centered design shapes XR input interaction and output perception so users can provide input and perceive output easily.

items.reason: Hardware, middleware, and the application layer are the three top-level components of an extended reality system; an input device is a component of hardware, not a top-level component.

items.reason: Effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction are the three measures of usability; context of use is the usage scenario in which usability is assessed, not a measure of usability.

items.reason: Users, goals, and context of use are the three crucial aspects of the ISO 9241-210-2009 usability definition; effectiveness is a measure of usability, not one of those crucial aspects.

questions.question: Why can interactive-system designers start from the novice, intermittent, and expert user categorization rather than always conducting field studies?
questions.reference_answer: Field studies are typically needed to understand users, but they are time-consuming, laborious, and require elaborate setup and planning, so designers can rely on the categorization as a starting point. Users in the novice, intermittent, and expert classes are likely to behave differently, which lets designers make broad interactive-system design decisions. The categorization is broad, but it is useful when the design process starts, while finer empirical categorizations are possible.

questions.question: How does user-centered design guide both input and output design in an extended reality system?
questions.reference_answer: Because an extended reality system is highly interactive, human factors are important for understanding how easily a user can provide input and perceive output. User-centered interaction design and user input modeling let the user provide input data seamlessly, effectively, and easily. Perceptual design and output modeling also require a user-centered approach because output stimuli must match the user's perception, so the user can perceive and understand the output.

questions.question: How does the International Standards Organization 9241-210-2009 definition connect a product's specified users, goals, and context of use with its usability measures?
questions.reference_answer: It defines usability as the extent to which specified users achieve specified goals with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a specified context of use. A usable product is therefore intended for a specified group of users, supports a specified set of goals, and is designed for a specified context of use. Effectiveness is whether the user can do what they want, efficiency is how fast, and satisfaction is how satisfied the user is.
